interpretation: Exact-zero breeding-component loss is usually persistent within the available Palmer and Signy follow-up windows.
The data do not support the proposed H>0 return-threshold hypothesis: the only completed return has H<0.
Because almost all loss spells occur during continuing decline, persistent vacancy alone cannot establish causal hysteresis.
Only one informative positive-background case revisits or exceeds the loss-state background while remaining empty, so a same-state recovery comparison is not identified in this data family.
next_valid_step: Use an independent penguin system that contains genuine decline-to-recovery trajectories with component-resolved occupancy and enough exact empty-to-reoccupied transitions; do not introduce low-count pseudo-absence thresholds to rescue the present data.
